title: Chemical-state-negative filtering proposes a product-qualified ribosomal display library
status_authority: Current scientific acceptance is conferred only by exact version-bound substantive internal review overlays; physical acquisition and novelty are separate.
reported_status: The source proposes encoding distinct nonstandard peptide products on separate mRNA templates, using established ribosomal elongation and mRNA-display linkage, then applying a downstream chemical-state-negative filter to a completed genotype-linked library. In its example, an uncyclized hydrazinoester product retains an exposed hydrazinyl nitrogen that can react with aldehyde, while the desired cyclic product has consumed that nitrogen. Marking/removing the linear products could qualify library members before functional selection. The source proposes adapting known hydrazone chemistry to intact mRNA fusions; selective capture in an RNA-compatible environment, fusion survival, side-reaction rates, and false tagging have not been demonstrated. The immobilized aldehyde scavenger is speculative.

proof_availability.classification_scope: Reviewed mechanism proposal for downstream qualification of a finished genotype-linked library, not acquired selective capture/display or step-by-step product gating. RNA compatibility, selective chemistry, distinguishable decoding registers and integrated performance remain open. The 22% substrate example is not the double-ring experiment.
